decisions.reason: Glass-silicon wafers with through contacts build on core polishing and drilling capabilities, and the advanced-packaging market is still developing, so keeping this low-cost option open is worth more than its carrying cost.
Carrier wafers for smaller diameters fit the firm's stated direction toward thin-wafer handling and reusable carriers, and they cost little to carry within the established offer.
The Cu-interposer is a flagship launched in 2019 in a growing glass-interposer market, so its uncertainty has not resolved and strategic commitment favors keeping it.
The Wafer Universe off-the-shelf brand is a flagship close to the core business with low incremental cost, and it broadens the firm's otherwise narrow range.
Glass-based circuit boards are distant from the core and could pull resources away, but glass substrates for electronics remain a promising and unresolved option, so it narrowly stays.
